podcast.title: Unreleased Sex Tape with Kid Rock (1999)
podcast.body: A 45-minute sex tape featuring Scott Stapp, Kid Rock, and four groupies, recorded in an RV or tour bus around 1999, was reportedly acquired by Red Light District (the company behind the Paris Hilton sex tape) in 2005. Despite their attempts to sell it, lawsuits prevented its official release, though it remains available on the internet. "It was the tape featuring Scott Stap of Creed and Kid Rock."

podcast.title: Fatherhood Hall of Fame Induction (2000)
podcast.body: The year after the sex tape was made (circa 1999), Scott Stapp was inducted as the first member of the Fatherhood Hall of Fame in 2000. This honor was created by WomenForFatherhood.org, an organization dedicated to recognizing "dedicated parents and strong role models," creating a notable contrast with the unreleased tape. "Scott Stap became the first inductee into the Fatherhood Hall of Fame, an honor created by a group called WomenForFatherhood.org."

podcast.title: Massive Sales with Creed, Low Solo Sales
podcast.body: While serving as the singer for Creed, Scott Stapp was part of a band that sold "tens of millions of records." However, his subsequent solo career saw "not a lot of single sold," indicating a significant drop in commercial success. "Tens of millions of records were sold when he was the singer with Creed, not a lot of single sold as a solo artist."

podcast.title: Solo Career Underperformance
podcast.body: Stapp's solo career has been largely unsuccessful, failing to replicate the commercial achievements he experienced with Creed. "And it hasn't been any better with his former bandmates."

xref.title: Sex Tape with Scott Stapp of Creed (1999, Florida) – Red Light District Attempted to Sell; Lawsuit Prevented Release
xref.body: In 2005, a company called Red Light District — the same distributor behind the Paris Hilton tape — came into possession of approximately 45 minutes of video footage from 1999, shot on tour in Florida, featuring Kid Rock and Creed singer Scott Stapp being pleasured by a series of groupies in a motor home. Red Light District would not confirm how they obtained the tape and intended to sell it. A lawsuit was filed and the tape was never officially released. The episode was further incongruous given that approximately six months before the tape emerged, in June 2000, Stapp had been named the first inductee into the Fatherhood Hall of Fame by the organization WomenForFatherhood.org. "Kid Rock and Scott Stapp have had a falling out."

xref.title: Confrontation with Fred Durst (Summer 2000)
xref.body: A concert in New York that summer saw Fred Durst of Limp Biscuit diss singer Scott Stapp, to which Stapp responded by challenging Durst to a boxing match. "Actually, the end of Creed involved a fight with Limp Biscuit. There was a concert in New York that summer, and Fred Durst discreed singer Scott Stapp, and Stapp responded by challenging Fred to a boxing match."

xref.title: Scott Stapp's Car Accident (July 2002)
xref.body: Stapp was involved in a car accident in July 2002, leading to the cancellation of a significant portion of a major tour. He was charged with reckless driving of his SUV. "Then Scott got into a car accident, July of 2002, forcing the cancellation of a good chunk of a big tour. Scott was charged with reckless driving of his SUV."

xref.title: Scott Stapp's Suicide Attempt (Late 2002/Early 2003)
xref.body: After consuming a large bottle of Jack Daniel's, Stapp put an "automatic type handgun that SWAT teams use" to his head but ultimately decided against taking his own life, realizing he had a son. This event was described as a potential "wake-up call" that was short-lived. "After a big bottle of Jack, he actually put a handgun, an automatic type that SWAT teams use. He put it up to his head before deciding that, you know what, I have a son, this is stupid, I'm not going to do it."

xref.title: OxyContin Addiction (Early 2004)
xref.body: By early 2004, Scott Stapp traveled to Maui where he became addicted to OxyContin, another powerful painkiller. "By early 2004, he went to Maui, where he was able to get himself addicted to oxy-contin, another powerful painkiller."

xref.title: Reunion Catalyst in Las Vegas (2008)
xref.body: In 2008, Scott Stapp and guitarist Mark Tremonti met at the Hard Rock Hotel in Las Vegas and decided to reunite, aiming to "set things right" and redefine Creed's legacy positively. "In 2008, Scott and guitars Mark Tramonty met up at the Hard Rock Hotel in Vegas, and they decided that it was time to get back together and set things right."

xref.title: Scott Stapp's Damaged Public Image
xref.body: Stapp's image as a virtuous father and husband was undermined by several incidents, including an accusation of throwing a bottle at his wife. "But then several things surfaced to make that image look hypocritical, including the time that he threw a bottle at his wife."

xref.title: Scott Stapp's Reflection on Hiatus
xref.body: Scott Stapp described the break from 2002 as "beneficial and necessary" for individual and collective growth, allowing them to build strong foundations with their families and for him, his faith. He felt they reconnected with the world and gained independent identities, viewing past conflicts as a "small chapter in a novel." "Well, you know, it's kind of a reintroduction, you know, is how the band would characterize it. I mean, it's almost a rebirth."

xref.title: Scott Stapp's Substance Abuse (Post-Accident)
xref.body: During his recovery from the car accident, Scott Stapp became addicted to the painkiller Percocet, also using Xanax for anxiety and panic attacks, and steroids for an inflamed throat, making him "kind of loopy," especially when mixed with alcohol. "During his recovery, Scott became addicted to the painkiller per cassette. Plus, there was the Xanax, which was supposed to help with anxiety and panic attacks. And he was on steroids for an inflamed throat. So, yeah, Scott got kind of loopy, especially when alcohol was added to the mix."
